Architectural Comparison & Layout Trade-offs Using a compound layout strategy maximizes usability: BorderLayout manages macro-level window structure, GridLayout(3, 2) guarantees that form input boxes align symmetrically with descriptive labels, and FlowLayout preserves the ergonomic proportions of push buttons without stretching them unnaturally.

title: Define multithreading.
chunks: Multithreading is a Java feature that enables concurrent execution of two or more parts of a single program (threads) to achieve maximum utilization of CPU cores. Each thread represents an independent, lightweight path of execution sharing common heap memory and process resources, but maintaining its own Program Counter (PC), registers, and call stack. // Spawning a concurrent thread new Thread(() -> System.out.println("Concurrent task executing")).start();

title: Name any two methods used to control thread execution.
chunks: Two fundamental methods of the java.lang.Thread class used to control thread execution are: sleep(long millis) : A static method that temporarily pauses the currently executing thread for a specified duration in milliseconds, transitioning it to the TIMED_WAITING state without releasing locks. join() : An instance method that causes the calling thread to wait until the target thread on which join() was called terminates.

title: Define a checked exception.
chunks: A checked exception in Java is an exception that is verified by the compiler at compile-time. Checked exceptions extend java.lang.Exception (excluding subclasses of RuntimeException ). The compiler mandates the "catch or declare" rule: methods that may trigger a checked exception must either catch it via a try-catch block or declare it using the throws keyword in the signature. Examples: IOException , SQLException , ClassNotFoundException .

title: Name the keyword used to explicitly throw an exception.
chunks: The keyword used to explicitly throw an exception in Java is throw . It is used inside method bodies followed by an instance of a Throwable class (or its subclasses): // Explicitly throwing an exception instance if (age < 18) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("Age must be at least 18."); } Note: Do not confuse throw (which throws an object) with throws (which declares potential exceptions in a method signature).

title: Define a thread in Java.
chunks: In Java, a thread is the smallest schedulable unit of CPU execution within a program. It is commonly described as a "lightweight process". Key Properties: Shared Heap: All threads within a Java Virtual Machine (JVM) process share common heap memory, static variables, and process resources. Private State: Each thread possesses its own private Call Stack, Program Counter (PC), and local register set. Creation Mechanisms: Created either by extending the java.lang.Thread class or by implementing the java.lang.Runnable interface. The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) thread scheduler assigns CPU timeslices to active threads based on thread priorities (ranging from Thread.MIN_PRIORITY = 1 to Thread.MAX_PRIORITY = 10 , default is 5).

title: List any two methods of the Thread class.
chunks: Two essential methods provided by the java.lang.Thread class are: public void start() : Allocates native system thread resources and creates a separate call stack. Transitions the thread into the RUNNABLE state and invokes the target's run() method asynchronously. public void run() : The entry point for the thread's execution containing the business logic. Overridden by developers to specify the operations executed by the new thread. Other essential methods include Thread.sleep(long millis) (pauses execution) and thread.join() (waits for thread termination). Method signatures are strictly defined in java.lang.Thread . Additionally, getPriority() and setPriority(int priority) inspect and configure thread execution priority within the host operating system.

title: Name two states in the life cycle of a thread.
chunks: The Java thread lifecycle (defined in Thread.State ) includes six distinct states. Two core states are: NEW: A thread is in this initial state after instantiation ( new Thread() ) but before the start() method has been invoked. No OS call stack has been allocated yet. RUNNABLE: After start() is invoked, the thread enters the RUNNABLE state. It is either executing instructions on a CPU core or waiting in the operating system ready queue for processor scheduling. Other states include: BLOCKED , WAITING , TIMED_WAITING , and TERMINATED . State transitions occur dynamically: invoking sleep() or wait() shifts a thread from RUNNABLE to TIMED_WAITING or WAITING . When the timer expires or notify() is called, the thread returns to RUNNABLE .

title: Define an exception in Java.
chunks: An exception in Java is an abnormal condition or event that occurs during program execution (runtime) and disrupts the standard sequential flow of instructions. Key Principles: Object Representation: Every exception is an instantiated object inheriting directly or indirectly from java.lang.Throwable . Encapsulation: The exception object encapsulates diagnostic state: the error type, descriptive message, and the snapshot execution call stack (stack trace). Handling: Java enables structured recovery through try , catch , finally , throw , and throws . Exceptions in Java represent recoverable operational faults (such as missing files or invalid network endpoints), in contrast to java.lang.Error which denotes catastrophic system failures (such as OutOfMemoryError ).

title: Name the purpose of try and catch blocks.
chunks: The try and catch blocks form Java's core mechanism for robust runtime exception handling: try Block Purpose: Encloses a section of "guarded" statements that might generate an abnormal condition or throw an exception during execution. If an exception occurs, the remaining statements in the try block are skipped. catch Block Purpose: Immediately follows the try block to intercept, identify, and handle the thrown exception object. It prevents abrupt JVM program termination and executes recovery or logging logic. try { int quotient = 100 / 0; // Risky code } catch (ArithmeticException e) { System.out.println("Caught and handled: " + e.getMessage()); // Graceful recovery }

title: Name two classes from the Java Collections Framework.
chunks: Two fundamental, widely-utilized classes from the Java Collections Framework (package java.util ) are: java.util.ArrayList : Implements the List interface backed by a resizable, dynamic array. Maintains insertion order, permits duplicate elements, and offers fast $O(1)$ random index access via get(int index) . java.util.HashSet : Implements the Set interface backed internally by a HashMap . Disallows duplicate elements, makes no guarantees regarding iteration order, and provides $O(1)$ average time complexity for basic operations ( add , remove , contains ). Both classes share common utility methods from the root Collection interface including size() , isEmpty() , clear() , and iterator() , but exhibit contrasting ordering and uniqueness semantics.

title: State one feature of a JavaBean.
chunks: A primary defining feature of a JavaBean is encapsulated properties with standardized accessors and mutators (getters and setters) . In accordance with the JavaBeans API specification, all class instance variables (properties) must be declared private , and accessed strictly through public methods following strict naming conventions: public class StudentBean implements java.io.Serializable { private String name; // Private property public String getName() { return name; } // Getter public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; } // Setter } Other key conventions: Must provide a public no-argument constructor and implement java.io.Serializable . Adhering to JavaBeans design patterns allows visual IDE builder tools and enterprise frameworks (such as Spring and Hibernate) to automatically inspect, instantiate, and inject bean properties using reflection.

title: Name the Java class commonly used to obtain the IP address of a host.
chunks: The standard Java class commonly used to encapsulate and obtain the IP address of a host is java.net.InetAddress . This class represents an Internet Protocol (IP) address for both 32-bit IPv4 and 128-bit IPv6 systems. Because it lacks public constructors, instances are created using factory methods: import java.net.InetAddress; // Obtain IP of a remote host InetAddress addr = InetAddress.getByName("www.google.com"); System.out.println("Host Name: " + addr.getHostName()); System.out.println("IP Address: " + addr.getHostAddress()); Key resolution methods include getHostAddress() , getHostName() , and getLocalHost() . The static method InetAddress.getAllByName(String host) returns an array containing all IP addresses associated with a multi-homed domain (such as major cloud load-balancers), handling DNS failover.

title: Explain the difference between start() and run().
chunks: The distinction between start() and run() is fundamental to multithreading in Java: Dimension start() Method run() Method Thread Creation Allocates a new operating system native thread and initializes a fresh private call stack. Does NOT create a new thread; executes strictly as a standard synchronous method call. Execution Context Executes concurrently in a newly spawned separate worker thread. Executes synchronously within the context of the currently calling thread (e.g., main ). Invocation Count Can only be invoked ONCE per thread instance; subsequent calls throw IllegalThreadStateException . Can be invoked repeatedly like any ordinary Java method. Thread t = new Thread(() -> System.out.println("Worker")); t.start(); // Creates new thread, executes concurrently t.run(); // Executes synchronously in the caller thread, no new thread!

title: Describe one advantage of implementing Runnable.
chunks: The primary advantage of implementing the Runnable interface over extending the Thread class is overcoming Java's single inheritance limitation . Because Java does not permit multiple class inheritance, a class that extends Thread cannot inherit from any other class. By implementing Runnable , your worker class preserves its single inheritance slot, enabling it to inherit from other domain classes or framework bases (such as extends Applet or extends JFrame ): // Can inherit from Frame AND execute as a concurrent thread public class GameWindow extends Frame implements Runnable { public void run() { // Game loop animation logic } } Additionally, it decouples task definition from thread execution mechanism, allowing use with modern thread pools ( ExecutorService ).

title: Explain why synchronization is used when threads share data.
chunks: Synchronization is required when concurrent threads share mutable data to prevent race conditions and data corruption . Technical Rationale: Race Conditions: When multiple threads read and write shared variables concurrently without coordination, non-atomic operations (such as count++ which entails read, modify, and write back) interleave unpredictably, resulting in lost updates. Mutual Exclusion (Mutex): Synchronization guarantees that only one thread can execute a critical section at any given instant by enforcing exclusive lock acquisition on the target object's monitor. Memory Visibility: Enforces a "happens-before" relationship, guaranteeing that changes written by one thread are flushed to main RAM and immediately visible to other threads.

title: Differentiate between checked and unchecked exceptions.
chunks: The distinction between checked and unchecked exceptions forms the backbone of Java's robust exception handling architecture: Feature Checked Exception Unchecked Exception Hierarchy Directly inherits from java.lang.Exception (excluding RuntimeException ). Inherits from java.lang.RuntimeException or java.lang.Error . Verification Time Verified at compile-time by the javac compiler. Ignored at compile-time; evaluated at runtime . Handling Rule Strictly mandatory: Must be enclosed in try-catch or declared with throws . Optional: Compiler does not force catching or declaring. Root Cause External environmental conditions beyond program control (missing files, network drop). Internal programming logic bugs (null references, bad array index, divide by zero). Examples IOException , SQLException , ClassNotFoundException . NullPointerException , ArithmeticException , IndexOutOfBoundsException .

title: Explain when a finally block is executed.
chunks: In Java, a finally block is guaranteed to execute under virtually all circumstances , regardless of whether an exception is thrown or caught within the preceding try and catch blocks. Execution Rules: Normal Flow: Executes immediately after the try block completes without errors. Handled Exception: Executes immediately after the matching catch block completes. Unhandled Exception: Executes before the uncaught exception propagates up the call stack to abort the thread. Return Statements: Even if try or catch executes a return , break , or continue statement, the finally block executes before the return actually resolves! Sole Exception: The only scenario where finally does not execute is if the JVM terminates abruptly via System.exit(0) or an OS-level fatal kill.

title: Describe one difference between ArrayList and HashSet.
chunks: The primary architectural difference between ArrayList and HashSet lies in their element uniqueness and ordering guarantees : Dimension java.util.ArrayList java.util.HashSet Interface & Duplicates Implements List . Allows duplicate elements freely. Implements Set . Disallows duplicate elements ; duplicate insertions are rejected. Ordering Maintains strict insertion order based on 0-based integer indices. Unordered ; makes no guarantees about element iteration sequence. Underlying Data Structure Dynamic resizable object array. Internal hash table (backed by a HashMap instance). List list = new ArrayList<>(List.of("A", "A", "B")); // Size: 3 (duplicates retained) Set set = new HashSet<>(List.of("A", "A", "B")); // Size: 2 (duplicate "A" filtered)

title: Write a short program that creates a thread by extending Thread and prints three messages.
chunks: The program below demonstrates thread creation by subclassing Thread , overriding run() , and invoking start() to execute three messages: // Custom thread subclass class MessagePrinterThread extends Thread { @Override public void run() { for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { System.out.println("Thread Message #" + i + " from " + getName()); } } } public class ThreadSubclassDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { // Instantiate and initiate thread execution MessagePrinterThread worker = new MessagePrinterThread(); worker.setName("Worker-Thread"); worker.start(); // Spawns thread and invokes run() } } Calling worker.start() creates the independent execution thread which runs the loop printing three messages asynchronously. Subclassing Thread binds the execution logic directly to the thread object. Calling worker.start() creates the native call stack, transitions the thread to RUNNABLE , and asynchronously executes the three output statements. The method Thread.currentThread() returns a reference to the actively running thread, allowing inspecting thread state, group, and alive status via isAlive() .

title: Create two threads using the Runnable interface and start them.
chunks: The code below demonstrates creating and launching two independent concurrent threads using the Runnable interface: class TaskWorker implements Runnable { private String taskName; public TaskWorker(String name) { this.taskName = name; } @Override public void run() { for (int i = 1; i <= 2; i++) { System.out.println(taskName + " executing step " + i); } } } public class TwoThreadsRunnableDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { // 1. Create Runnable task instances Runnable task1 = new TaskWorker("Task-Alpha"); Runnable task2 = new TaskWorker("Task-Beta"); // 2. Wrap tasks in Thread objects Thread t1 = new Thread(task1); Thread t2 = new Thread(task2); // 3. Launch both threads concurrently t1.start(); t2.start(); } } By passing distinct Runnable instances (or the same instance) into new Thread(task) , both threads execute concurrently on separate call stacks, sharing CPU timeslices without blocking the main application thread. Using Runnable promotes clean architecture by separating the executable business task from the underlying system thread resource allocation, enabling seamless integration with Java thread pools like Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2) .

title: Use sleep() in a thread program to pause execution briefly between messages.
chunks: The program below utilizes Thread.sleep() to introduce a 1000-millisecond delay between sequential console messages, properly catching InterruptedException : public class SleepDemoThread extends Thread { @Override public void run() { String[] alerts = {"System Initializing...", "Connecting to Server...", "Ready for Commands."}; for (String msg : alerts) { System.out.println(msg); try { // Pause current thread for 1000 milliseconds (1 second) Thread.sleep(1000); } catch (InterruptedException e) { System.err.println("Thread sleep was interrupted: " + e.getMessage()); } } } public static void main(String[] args) { new SleepDemoThread().start(); } } Thread.sleep() places the calling thread in the TIMED_WAITING state while maintaining all acquired synchronization locks. If another active thread invokes interrupt() on the sleeping thread, Thread.sleep() immediately terminates the sleep interval, clears the interrupt status, and throws InterruptedException for graceful handling.

title: Write a program that handles division by zero using try-catch-finally.
chunks: The following program intercepts an illegal arithmetic division by zero using structured try-catch-finally blocks: public class DivisionByZeroHandling { public static void main(String[] args) { int numerator = 50; int denominator = 0; try { System.out.println("Attempting division: " + numerator + " / " + denominator); int result = numerator / denominator; // Triggers ArithmeticException System.out.println("Result: " + result); } catch (ArithmeticException e) { System.err.println("Exception Caught: Division by zero is undefined! (" + e.getMessage() + ")"); } finally { System.out.println("Finally block executed: Math operations finalized and resources closed."); } System.out.println("Program resumed normal execution."); } } When denominator is 0, the JVM instantiates and throws an ArithmeticException , bypassing the second print in try , jumping into catch , and finally executing the mandatory cleanup block.

title: Use ArrayList to add, remove, and display three city names.
chunks: The following code demonstrates core manipulation methods ( add , remove , and iteration) using java.util.ArrayList : import java.util.ArrayList; public class CityArrayListDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { // Instantiate a generic ArrayList of Strings ArrayList cities = new ArrayList<>(); // 1. Add three city names cities.add("Mumbai"); cities.add("Bengaluru"); cities.add("New Delhi"); System.out.println("Initial List: " + cities); // 2. Remove one city (by value or index) cities.remove("Mumbai"); System.out.println("After removing Mumbai: " + cities); // 3. Display remaining cities using an enhanced for-loop System.out.println("Displaying remaining cities:"); for (String city : cities) { System.out.println(" - " + city); } } } Calling cities.remove("Mumbai") shifts subsequent elements left to close the gap, maintaining contiguous storage in $O(n)$ time while preserving the insertion order of Bengaluru and New Delhi.

title: Write a program using HashMap to store three student roll numbers and names, then display them.
chunks: The program below demonstrates key-value pair association using java.util.HashMap where student roll numbers (Keys) map to student names (Values): import java.util.HashMap; import java.util.Map; public class StudentHashMapDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { // Create a HashMap with Integer keys and String values HashMap studentMap = new HashMap<>(); // Store three key-value pairs studentMap.put(101, "Alice Smith"); studentMap.put(102, "Bob Johnson"); studentMap.put(103, "Charlie Davis"); // Iterate and display entries using entrySet() System.out.println("--- Student Directory ---"); for (Map.Entry entry : studentMap.entrySet()) { System.out.println("Roll Number: " + entry.getKey() + " | Name: " + entry.getValue()); } } } HashMap provides $O(1)$ average time complexity for put() and get() via hash buckets.

title: Explain the difference between the NEW and RUNNABLE thread states.
chunks: The transition from NEW to RUNNABLE marks the birth and activation of a thread in the JVM lifecycle: Feature NEW State RUNNABLE State Lifecycle Point The thread object has been created via new Thread() , but start() has NOT yet been called. The start() method has been invoked on the thread instance. OS Resource Allocation Pure Java heap object only; no native operating system thread or call stack has been allocated. Native OS thread and private call stack are fully allocated and initialized. CPU Eligibility Ineligible for CPU execution. Actively running instructions on a CPU core or waiting in the OS ready queue for a timeslice.

title: Describe why the join() method is used in multithreaded programs.
chunks: The join() method in java.lang.Thread is used to achieve thread synchronization and deterministic execution ordering . Why It Is Used: Dependency Coordination: When a master thread (e.g. main ) spawns background worker threads to perform calculations or fetch data, it cannot process the final results until those workers finish. Execution Blocking: Invoking workerThread.join() forces the current thread to pause execution and enter the WAITING state until workerThread completely terminates. Eliminates Race Conditions: Guarantees that asynchronous tasks complete in deterministic sequence without inefficient busy-waiting loops. Thread worker = new Thread(() -> computeResults()); worker.start(); worker.join(); // Main thread pauses until worker terminates printSummary(); // Safe to use worker's output!

title: Differentiate between throw and throws.
chunks: While syntactically similar, throw and throws fulfill complementary roles in Java's exception handling system: Characteristic throw Keyword throws Keyword Purpose Used to explicitly throw an instantiated exception object. Used to declare the types of exceptions a method might throw to its caller. Location Inside method bodies or initializer blocks. Appended to the method signature declaration. Syntax Followed by an instance : throw new IOException(); Followed by class names : throws IOException, SQLException Quantity Can only throw one exception object at a time. Can declare multiple comma-separated exception classes. In summary: throw is an action verb that launches an exception from a method body, whereas throws is an informational clause that transfers exception-handling responsibility to the caller.

title: Explain why multiple catch blocks may be used with one try block.
chunks: Multiple catch blocks are associated with a single try block to provide specialized, granular recovery handling for diverse exception types that could arise within a complex block of code. Key Principles: Differentiated Recovery: A file processing block might throw FileNotFoundException (requiring a file-chooser prompt), NumberFormatException (requiring default value substitution), or SQLException (triggering a transaction rollback). Separate catch blocks permit distinct recovery logic for each. Subclass-to-Superclass Ordering Rule: Catch blocks are evaluated sequentially from top to bottom. Specific subclass exceptions must precede broader superclasses (e.g., ArithmeticException must appear before Exception ); otherwise, the compiler flags unreachable code. Java 7 introduced multi-catch syntax (e.g. catch (ArithmeticException | ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException e) ) to handle multiple independent exceptions with identical recovery logic without code duplication.

title: Describe the purpose of the synchronized keyword.
chunks: The synchronized keyword in Java provides language-level mutual exclusion (mutex) and thread safety when concurrent threads access shared resources. Core Capabilities: Monitor Lock Acquisition: Every Java object possesses an intrinsic monitor lock. When a thread enters a synchronized method or block, it acquires this lock. Any other thread attempting to access synchronized code on the same object is blocked until the lock is released. Critical Section Protection: Prevents race conditions and thread interleaving during non-atomic read-modify-write sequences. Memory Visibility: Enforces memory synchronization by flushing thread local CPU caches to shared RAM upon acquiring and releasing the lock. Synchronization can be applied to instance methods, static methods (locking the class object), or synchronized statements with explicit lock objects: synchronized(lockObject) { ... } for fine-grained concurrency control.

title: Explain the difference between ArrayList and LinkedList.
chunks: While both ArrayList and LinkedList implement the List interface, their internal memory architectures yield radically different performance profiles: Factor ArrayList LinkedList Underlying Structure Dynamic resizable array (contiguous memory). Doubly-linked list (nodes with data, prev, next pointers). Random Access ( get(i) ) Fast $O(1)$ : Direct memory address calculation. Slow $O(n)$ : Must traverse pointers from head/tail. Insertion / Deletion Slow $O(n)$ in middle: Requires array element shifting. Fast $O(1)$ once node position is reached: Simply updates pointers. Memory Overhead Low: Stores only elements and small reserve capacity. High: Stores two pointer references ( prev , next ) per element. In practice, ArrayList is preferred for read-heavy operations with frequent indexing, while LinkedList is optimal for queue or deque implementations requiring frequent insertions and deletions at boundaries.

title: Write a program to create a thread by implementing Runnable. Print five numbers from the run() method.
chunks: Implementing the Runnable interface represents the industry-standard architectural pattern for multithreading in Java, establishing a clean separation between task execution logic and JVM thread lifecycle management.

Program Implementation // 1. Define task logic by implementing Runnable class NumberSequenceTask implements Runnable { @Override public void run() { System.out.println("Worker thread initiated: " + Thread.currentThread().getName()); for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { System.out.println("[" + Thread.currentThread().getName() + "] Sequence Number: " + i); try { // Brief pause to simulate computational work Thread.sleep(300); } catch (InterruptedException e) { System.err.println("Thread interrupted: " + e.getMessage()); } } System.out.println("Worker thread finished: " + Thread.currentThread().getName()); } } public class RunnableThreadDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Main thread starting execution..."); // 2. Instantiate the task target NumberSequenceTask task = new NumberSequenceTask(); // 3. Wrap task inside Thread instance and assign descriptive name Thread workerThread = new Thread(task, "NumberWorker-1"); // 4. Initiate thread execution via start() workerThread.start(); System.out.println("Main thread continues independent operations..."); } }

Architectural Highlights & Execution Flow Separation of Concerns: Runnable encapsulates the computational unit of work (the "what"), while Thread manages OS thread allocation and scheduling (the "how"). Single Inheritance Preservation: Because Java disallows multiple class inheritance, implementing Runnable preserves the class's ability to extend other domain bases (e.g. extends JPanel implements Runnable ). Execution Lifecycle: Calling workerThread.start() creates a new native OS call stack, transitions the thread into the RUNNABLE state, and asynchronously invokes run() to print numbers 1 through 5. Thread Pool Compatibility: Runnable instances can be directly submitted to modern Java concurrency utilities such as ExecutorService .

Detailed Step-by-Step Program Walkthrough 1. Implementing Runnable: The class NumberSequenceTask implements the functional interface Runnable by providing the concrete implementation of its single abstract method run() . 2. Thread Construction: In main() , an instance of NumberSequenceTask is passed to the Thread(Runnable target, String name) constructor. This associates the execution logic with the newly created thread. 3. Thread Execution Lifecycle: Calling workerThread.start() signals the JVM to request a new operating system thread, initialize a dedicated call stack, and call run() asynchronously. Inside run() , the for-loop executes five iterations, pausing for 300ms between numbers using Thread.sleep() .

title: Write a Java program that starts two threads and uses join() so the main thread waits for both to finish.
chunks: The program below demonstrates thread lifecycle synchronization where the primary main thread spawns two concurrent worker threads and halts using join() until both workers terminate: class WorkerService extends Thread { private int durationMillis; public WorkerService(String name, int durationMillis) { super(name); this.durationMillis = durationMillis; } @Override public void run() { System.out.println("[" + getName() + "] Task started (duration: " + durationMillis + "ms)"); try { Thread.sleep(durationMillis); } catch (InterruptedException e) { System.err.println("[" + getName() + "] Interrupted!"); } System.out.println("[" + getName() + "] Task FINISHED successfully."); } } public class ThreadJoinSynchronizationDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Main thread: Launching worker threads..."); WorkerService workerA = new WorkerService("Worker-A", 1200); WorkerService workerB = new WorkerService("Worker-B", 800); // Start both threads concurrently workerA.start(); workerB.start(); try { System.out.println("Main thread: Waiting for Worker-A and Worker-B to terminate..."); workerA.join(); // Main blocks until workerA completes workerB.join(); // Main blocks until workerB completes } catch (InterruptedException e) { System.err.println("Main thread interrupted while waiting: " + e.getMessage()); } System.out.println("Main thread: All worker threads have finished. Aggregating results and exiting."); } } Synchronization Mechanics: Without join() , the main thread would print its termination statement immediately while workers were still processing in the background.

State Transition Analysis during join() When the main thread calls workerA.join() , the JVM transitions the main thread from RUNNABLE into the WAITING state, relinquishing CPU scheduling. Once workerA completes its run() method and enters TERMINATED , the JVM notifies and resumes the main thread, which then checks workerB.join() before proceeding to final summary output.

title: Create a program with two threads that print their names and demonstrate the use of setName() and getName().
chunks: Assigning descriptive, readable names to concurrent threads is essential for multi-threaded debugging, production logging, and thread dump inspection. The program below demonstrates naming threads using setName() and querying identities via getName() .

Program Implementation class NamedWorkerThread extends Thread { public NamedWorkerThread(String initialName) { super(initialName); } @Override public void run() { // Query active thread identity inside the execution loop System.out.println("run() executing on thread -> " + getName()); for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { System.out.println("[" + getName() + "] Processing computational batch #" + i); try { Thread.sleep(250); } catch (InterruptedException e) { System.err.println("[" + getName() + "] Interrupted!"); } } System.out.println("[" + getName() + "] Task finished."); } } public class ThreadNamingDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { // Instantiate two threads with default names NamedWorkerThread t1 = new NamedWorkerThread("Default-1"); NamedWorkerThread t2 = new NamedWorkerThread("Default-2"); System.out.println("Original Name of T1: " + t1.getName()); System.out.println("Original Name of T2: " + t2.getName()); // Explicitly reassign descriptive operational names t1.setName("DatabaseSync-Thread"); t2.setName("FileExport-Thread"); System.out.println("Updated Name of T1: " + t1.getName()); System.out.println("Updated Name of T2: " + t2.getName()); // Launch concurrent execution t1.start(); t2.start(); } }

Technical Significance & Diagnostics Default Naming: When names are omitted, the JVM assigns sequential generic names such as Thread-0 , Thread-1 , which obscure error sources in production logs. Runtime Mutability: setName(String name) can be invoked before or during thread execution, allowing threads to update their names to reflect active processing tasks. Thread Dumps & Profilers: In enterprise diagnostics (via jstack or VisualVM), custom names allow administrators to instantly pinpoint blocked, deadlocked, or resource-heavy worker threads.

Step-by-Step Execution Walkthrough 1. Default Naming: When threads are instantiated without explicit names, the JVM assigns automatic identifiers (such as Thread-0 and Thread-1 ). Calling getName() reads this value. 2. Renaming Threads: The method t1.setName("DatabaseSync-Thread") modifies the thread's internal name string attribute. This can be called at any point during thread existence. 3. Diagnostic Logging: Inside run() , printing getName() confirms that each concurrent worker prints its custom descriptive name during each batch iteration, ensuring full traceability in application log files. Additionally, Thread.currentThread().getId() returns the positive long integer assigned as the unique thread identifier for the lifetime of the JVM thread.

title: Write a program that handles NumberFormatException when converting user input into an integer.
chunks: The program below demonstrates robust conversion of string input into numeric integer primitives using Integer.parseInt() while guarding against malformed inputs via NumberFormatException : import java.util.Scanner; public class NumberFormatSafeParser { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in); String[] testInputs = {"42", "3.1415", "one-hundred", "99999"}; for (String rawInput : testInputs) { System.out.println(" Evaluating input string: "" + rawInput + """); try { // Parsing attempt (throws NumberFormatException if non-integer characters exist) int parsedValue = Integer.parseInt(rawInput.trim()); int square = parsedValue * parsedValue; System.out.println("Success! Parsed integer: " + parsedValue + " (Square: " + square + ")"); } catch (NumberFormatException nfe) { System.err.println("NumberFormatException Caught: Cannot parse "" + rawInput + "" into an integer."); System.err.println("Diagnostic Reason: " + nfe.getMessage()); } finally { System.out.println("Finished parsing cycle for: "" + rawInput + """); } } scanner.close(); } } Root Cause: NumberFormatException is an unchecked exception (subclass of IllegalArgumentException ) thrown when a string contains invalid radix characters, decimal points, or values outside the 32-bit signed integer range ($-2^{31}$ to $2^{31}-1$).

Radix Parsing Mechanics & Boundary Validation Integer.parseInt(s) validates that the string consists solely of an optional ASCII sign ( + or - ) followed by decimal digits. If the input contains letters, decimal points (e.g. "3.14" ), spaces, or values exceeding signed 32-bit limits ($[-2^{31}, 2^{31}-1]$), it throws NumberFormatException , ensuring corrupt data never enters the domain model. In real-world applications, input parsing is wrapped in loop validation so users are prompted repeatedly until they supply a clean, valid integer. Proper exception handling prevents application crashes and provides clear diagnostics to end users.

title: Create a user-defined InvalidAgeException and throw it when the entered age is below 18.
chunks: User-defined (custom) exceptions enhance enterprise application architecture by creating domain-specific error types that capture business rule violations. The program below defines InvalidAgeException to enforce voting eligibility validation.

Program Implementation // 1. Custom checked exception extending java.lang.Exception class InvalidAgeException extends Exception { private int rejectedAge; public InvalidAgeException(String message, int age) { super(message); // Passes error message to Throwable this.rejectedAge = age; } public int getRejectedAge() { return rejectedAge; } } public class VoterEligibilityChecker { // 2. Declare custom exception in method signature using 'throws' public static void validateAge(int age) throws InvalidAgeException { if (age < 18) { // 3. Explicitly throw custom exception instance using 'throw' throw new InvalidAgeException("Voting Ineligible: Age must be 18 or older.", age); } else { System.out.println("Verification Passed: Age " + age + " is eligible to vote!"); } } public static void main(String[] args) { int[] testAges = {21, 15, 18, 12}; for (int age : testAges) { System.out.println(" Validating applicant with age: " + age); try { validateAge(age); } catch (InvalidAgeException ex) { System.err.println("CUSTOM EXCEPTION CAUGHT: " + ex.getMessage()); System.err.println("Rejected Invalid Value: " + ex.getRejectedAge() + " years old."); } } } }

Design Standards for Custom Exceptions Checked vs Unchecked Choice: Extending java.lang.Exception creates a checked exception, forcing callers to implement recovery logic. Extending RuntimeException creates an unchecked business exception. Constructor Delegation: Invoking super(message) initializes the standard message and captures the JVM execution call stack for diagnostics. Diagnostic State: Custom fields (such as rejectedAge ) store the illegal data payload for logging and forensic error auditing.

Step-by-Step Execution Walkthrough 1. Custom Exception Class: InvalidAgeException extends java.lang.Exception , designating it as a checked exception that the compiler requires callers to handle. 2. Method Declaration: validateAge(int age) throws InvalidAgeException declares that this method may throw the custom exception if the business rule is violated. 3. Throwing & Catching: When age is below 18, throw new InvalidAgeException(...) halts the method and creates an exception instance with diagnostic payload. In main() , the catch block intercepts it, prints the diagnostic message via ex.getMessage() , and logs the rejected age via ex.getRejectedAge() . This ensures business domain constraints are strictly validated before processing critical operations.

title: Write a program with multiple catch blocks to handle ArithmeticException and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
chunks: The program below demonstrates multiple distinct catch blocks attached to a single guarded try region, following strict subclass-to-superclass hierarchy ordering: public class MultiCatchDemonstration { public static void main(String[] args) { int[] data = {10, 20, 30}; // Scenario 1: ArithmeticException trigger executeOperation(data, 0, 1); // Scenario 2: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException trigger executeOperation(data, 2, 8); // Scenario 3: Valid execution executeOperation(data, 2, 0); } public static void executeOperation(int[] arr, int divisor, int arrayIndex) { System.out.println(" --- Executing with divisor=" + divisor + ", index=" + arrayIndex + " ---"); try { int value = arr[arrayIndex]; // May throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException int result = value / divisor; // May throw ArithmeticException System.out.println("Computation Successful! Result: " + result); } catch (ArithmeticException ae) { System.err.println("ArithmeticException Handler: Cannot divide by zero! (" + ae.getMessage() + ")"); } catch (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException aiobe) { System.err.println("ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException Handler: Invalid index " + arrayIndex + "! Array length is " + arr.length); } catch (Exception genericEx) { // General fallback handler (MUST be placed last) System.err.println("General Exception Handler: " + genericEx.getMessage()); } finally { System.out.println("Execution cycle completed."); } } } Crucial Java Rule: Specific subclasses ( ArithmeticException , ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException ) MUST precede broader parent classes ( Exception ). Reversing this order produces a compile-time error: "exception has already been caught" .

Compile-Time Reachability Invariants The Java compiler enforces strict reachability rules for multi-catch hierarchies: if a superclass handler appears before a subclass handler (e.g. placing catch (Exception e) ahead of catch (ArithmeticException ae) ), compilation fails with "exception ArithmeticException has already been caught" . Placing specific subclasses first guarantees correct dispatch.

title: Demonstrate synchronized access to a shared bank account balance using a synchronized method.
chunks: Concurrent manipulation of financial balances without thread synchronization causes lost updates and race conditions. The program below uses a synchronized method to enforce mutual exclusion: class BankAccount { private int balance = 1000; // Synchronized method locks 'this' monitor object public synchronized void withdraw(String customer, int amount) { System.out.println("[" + customer + "] Checking balance... Current: $" + balance); if (balance >= amount) { try { // Simulate processing latency Thread.sleep(200); } catch (InterruptedException e) {} balance -= amount; System.out.println("[" + customer + "] Successfully withdrew $" + amount + ". Remaining: $" + balance); } else { System.out.println("[" + customer + "] Transaction REJECTED! Insufficient funds for $" + amount); } } public int getBalance() { return balance; } } public class BankSyncDemo { public static void main(String[] args) { BankAccount sharedAccount = new BankAccount(); // Two customer threads accessing the SAME account Thread cust1 = new Thread(() -> sharedAccount.withdraw("Alice", 700)); Thread cust2 = new Thread(() -> sharedAccount.withdraw("Bob", 700)); cust1.start(); cust2.start(); } } Monitor Lock Operation: When Alice enters withdraw() , she acquires the intrinsic lock on sharedAccount . Bob is blocked in the BLOCKED state until Alice completes and exits the method, preventing double-withdrawal ($1400 withdrawn from a $1000 balance).

Mutual Exclusion Invariants & Atomicity Without synchronized , thread interleaving creates a critical race condition: both threads read balance = 1000 , pass the check, and deduct $700, reducing the balance to -$400. The synchronized keyword serializes execution: Alice acquires the monitor lock, completes the deduction, and releases the lock before Bob is permitted entry.

title: Use HashMap to store subject codes and subject names, then search for and display one subject by its code.
chunks: A java.util.HashMap associates unique keys with values using hash table indexing. The following program indexes subject codes and performs $O(1)$ fast lookups: import java.util.HashMap; import java.util.Scanner; public class SubjectCatalogLookup { public static void main(String[] args) { // 1. Create HashMap: Key = Course Code (String), Value = Course Name (String) HashMap courseCatalog = new HashMap<>(); // 2. Populate subject mappings courseCatalog.put("26UITU030005", "Operating Systems"); courseCatalog.put("26UITU030006", "Object Oriented Programming with Java"); courseCatalog.put("26UITU030007", "Database Management Systems"); courseCatalog.put("26UITU030008", "Design and Analysis of Algorithms"); courseCatalog.put("26UITU030009", "Discrete Mathematics"); System.out.println("Total courses indexed: " + courseCatalog.size()); // 3. Search and display subjects by code String searchCode = "26UITU030006"; searchSubject(courseCatalog, searchCode); // Search for a non-existent code searchSubject(courseCatalog, "INVALID_CODE_99"); } public static void searchSubject(HashMap map, String code) { System.out.println(" Querying Catalog for Subject Code: [" + code + "]"); // Fast O(1) containment check if (map.containsKey(code)) { String subjectName = map.get(code); System.out.println(" MATCH FOUND: Code " + code + " -> " + subjectName); } else { System.err.println(" NOT FOUND: Subject code '" + code + "' does not exist in catalog."); } } } Technical Mechanics: containsKey() computes the hash of the search key to pinpoint the specific bucket index, achieving constant-time $O(1)$ search performance.

Internal Hash Table Mechanics & Complexity When courseCatalog.get(code) is called, the JVM computes the hash code of the string key via hashCode() and maps it to a hash bucket index via modulo arithmetic. In the absence of hash collisions, retrieval executes in constant $O(1)$ time, vastly outperforming linear search on lists. Additionally, getOrDefault(key, defaultValue) avoids null pointer risks by returning a predefined fallback if the course code is missing.

title: Write a Java program using InetAddress to obtain and display both the host name and IP address of a given host.
chunks: The java.net.InetAddress class encapsulates both high-level domain hostnames and their underlying IP addresses (IPv4 / IPv6). The program below resolves remote and local network identities: import java.net.InetAddress; import java.net.UnknownHostException; public class NetworkHostResolver { public static void main(String[] args) { String targetDomain = "www.google.com"; // 1. Resolve Remote Host try { System.out.println("Resolving remote domain: " + targetDomain + "..."); InetAddress remoteHost = InetAddress.getByName(targetDomain); System.out.println("--- Remote Host Details ---"); System.out.println("Canonical Host Name : " + remoteHost.getCanonicalHostName()); System.out.println("Resolved Host Name : " + remoteHost.getHostName()); System.out.println("IP Address String : " + remoteHost.getHostAddress()); // 2. Resolve Local Machine Information InetAddress localMachine = InetAddress.getLocalHost(); System.out.println(" --- Local Machine Details ---"); System.out.println("Local Host Name : " + localMachine.getHostName()); System.out.println("Local IP Address : " + localMachine.getHostAddress()); } catch (UnknownHostException uhe) { System.err.println("DNS Resolution Failure: Host could not be located -> " + uhe.getMessage()); } } } Networking Lifecycle: InetAddress.getByName(host) performs an asynchronous DNS lookup via native OS resolver APIs. If the hostname cannot be mapped to an IP address, it throws the checked UnknownHostException . getHostAddress() returns the dotted-quad textual IP representation.

DNS Resolution & Network Protocol Integration InetAddress interfaces with underlying operating system socket libraries and DNS servers. When getByName() resolves a domain, it queries local hosts files and configured DNS resolvers. In enterprise network programming, InetAddress instances are passed directly to Socket and ServerSocket constructors for TCP/IP network communication. The method isReachable(timeoutMillis) sends ICMP echo requests (or establishes a TCP connection on port 7) to verify if the remote host is currently reachable over the network.

title: Create a simple JavaBean named StudentBean with private fields, a no-argument constructor, getters, and setters.
chunks: A JavaBean is a standard reusable software component adhering to three strict architectural conventions: encapsulation (private fields), public default constructor, and standardized accessor/mutator methods. import java.io.Serializable; // 1. JavaBean class must implement Serializable public class StudentBean implements Serializable { private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L; // 2. Private properties (encapsulation) private int studentId; private String studentName; private double cgpa; // 3. Mandatory public no-argument constructor public StudentBean() { this.studentId = 0; this.studentName = "Unknown"; this.cgpa = 0.0; } // Optional parameterized constructor for convenient initialization public StudentBean(int studentId, String studentName, double cgpa) { this.studentId = studentId; this.studentName = studentName; this.cgpa = cgpa; } // 4. Standard Getters (Accessors) and Setters (Mutators) public int getStudentId() { return studentId; } public void setStudentId(int studentId) { this.studentId = studentId; } public String getStudentName() { return studentName; } public void setStudentName(String studentName) { this.studentName = studentName; } public double getCgpa() { return cgpa; } public void setCgpa(double cgpa) { this.cgpa = cgpa; } @Override public String toString() { return "StudentBean [ID=" + studentId + ", Name=" + studentName + ", CGPA=" + cgpa + "]"; } } Conventions Justification: The no-argument constructor enables reflection frameworks (Spring, JSP, Hibernate) to instantiate beans dynamically via Class.newInstance() ; getters/setters enable automated property introspection.

JavaBeans Enterprise Framework Integration The standard naming conventions of JavaBeans enable reflection-driven frameworks (such as Spring BeanFactory, Hibernate ORM, and Jakarta Enterprise Beans) to dynamically discover properties via java.beans.Introspector . Implementing Serializable ensures the bean can be persisted to disk or transmitted over network sockets.

Unit I: Java Basics Programming paradigm and name any two programming paradigms other than OOP A programming paradigm is a fundamental style or approach to programming, dictating how tasks are structured and executed. Two other paradigms besides Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) are: Procedural Programming (e.g., C) Functional Programming (e.g., Haskell, LISP) When was Java officially announced by Sun Microsystems, and what was its original name Java was officially announced by Sun Microsystems in 1995 . Its original name during development was Oak (named after an oak tree outside James Gosling's office). Procedural and object-oriented programming Procedural Programming (POP) Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Program is divided into small parts called functions . Program is divided into parts called objects . Follows a Top-Down approach. Follows a Bottom-Up approach. Data is freely moving and less secure. Data is hidden (encapsulated) and highly secure. Example: C, Pascal Example: Java, C++, Python JDK, JRE, and JVM JDK (Java Development Kit): A full software development environment. It contains the JRE plus development tools like the compiler ( javac ) and debugger. JRE (Java Runtime Environment): The environment required to run Java programs. It contains the JVM and core class libraries. JVM (Java Virtual Machine): An abstract machine

that executes Java Bytecode. It makes Java platform-independent. Bytecode, and why is Java considered platform-independent Bytecode is a highly optimized set of instructions generated by the Java compiler ( javac ) after compiling the source code. It is not machine code, but rather intermediate code. Java is platform-independent because the compiler generates this bytecode instead of native machine code. This bytecode can be executed on any operating system as long as that system has a JVM (Java Virtual Machine) installed to interpret it (Write Once, Run Anywhere). Inheritance: A mechanism where a new class (child) inherits properties and behaviors from an existing class (parent), promoting code reusability. the four access modifiers in Java and state the default access level The four access modifiers in Java (from most restrictive to least) are: private (accessible only within the same class) default (no keyword; accessible only within the same package) protected (accessible within the same package and subclasses in other packages) public (accessible from anywhere) If no modifier is specified, the access level is default (package-private). Class and what is an object in Java A class is a user-defined blueprint or prototype from which objects are created. An object is a runtime instance of a class that has state and behavior. Difference: A class is a logical entity that consumes no memory upon declaration, whereas an object is a physical entity that consumes memory space in the heap when instantiated. Purpose of the new keyword in Java The new keyword in Java is used to create a new object or array by allocating memory at runtime. It essentially instantiates a class. Purpose of the this keyword in Java The this keyword is a reference variable that refers to the current object on which the method or constructor is being invoked. Autoboxing and unboxing in Java Autoboxing: The automatic

conversion that the Java compiler makes between the primitive types and their corresponding object wrapper classes (e.g., converting int to Integer ). Unboxing: The reverse process; converting an object of a wrapper type back to its corresponding primitive value (e.g., converting Integer to int ). String immutability String immutability means that once a String object is created, its value or state cannot be changed. Types supported in Java (via classes): Single Inheritance Multilevel Inheritance Hierarchical Inheritance (Note: Multiple and Hybrid inheritance are not supported through classes, only through interfaces). Purpose of the super keyword The super keyword is a reference variable used to refer to the immediate parent class object. Two Methods: toString() equals(Object obj) Polymorphism Polymorphism is the ability of an object or method to take on many forms, allowing the

same interface to be used for different underlying forms (data types). Two Types: Compile-time Polymorphism (Static binding, e.g., Method Overloading). Run-time Polymorphism (Dynamic binding, e.g., Method Overriding). Dynamic binding Dynamic Binding is the process where the compiler does not resolve the method call at compile time, but rather the JVM determines the actual method implementation to execute at runtime based on the actual object type. It is called late binding because the binding of the method call to the method body is delayed until the program is actually executing. Upcasting and downcasting in Java Upcasting: Casting a subclass reference variable to a superclass reference. This is done automatically and implicitly by the compiler. Downcasting: Casting a superclass reference variable back to a subclass reference. This must be done explicitly by the programmer and requires checking to prevent ClassCastException . Purpose of the instanceof operator The instanceof operator is a binary operator used to test whether a given object is an instance of a specific class, subclass, or interface. A. (Dog and Cat both inherit Animal) Hybrid: A combination of two or more types. Method overloading and method overriding Method Overloading Method Overriding Occurs within the same class . Occurs between parent and child classes. Parameters must be different. (Dynamic Binding). The compiler knows exactly which method to call based on the method signature (number and type of arguments). Fast execution because binding happens early. Run-time Polymorphism: Achieved through Method Overriding. A parent reference points to a child object. The JVM determines which overridden method to execute during runtime based on the actual object type , not the reference type. Dynamic binding and object casting Dynamic Binding is resolving a method call at runtime depending on the actual object. Upcasting: Casting a subclass to a superclass. It is automatic. so the JVM resolves it during execution. class Vehicle { void move() { System.out.println("Moving"); } } class Car extends Vehicle { @Override void move() { System.out.println("Driving on wheels"); } } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Vehicle v = new Car(); // Superclass ref, Subclass object v.move(); // Outputs: Driving on wheels } } At compile time, the compiler ensures move() exists in Vehicle . At runtime, the JVM notices the object is actually a Car and executes the overridden version. Object casting in Java class Animal {} class Dog extends Animal { void bark() { System.out.println("Woof"); } } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { // Upcasting (Automatic) Animal a = new Dog(); // Downcasting (Explicit & requires checking) if (a instanceof Dog) { Dog d = (Dog) a; d.bark(); // Safe to call child-specific method } } } Abstract classes in Java abstract class Shape { Shape() { System.out.println("Shape created"); } // Abstract method (no body) abstract void draw(); // Concrete method void display() { System.out.println("Displaying shape"); } } class Circle extends Shape { @Override void draw() { System.out.println("Drawing Circle"); } } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args)

{ Shape s = new Circle(); s.display(); s.draw(); } } Interfaces in Java and compare them Interfaces define contracts (mostly abstract methods). Unlike Abstract classes which can have state and constructors, interfaces cannot maintain instance state. interface Printable { void print(); } interface Showable { void show(); } class Document implements Printable, Showable { public void print() { System.out.println("Printing"); } public void show() { System.out.println("Showing"); } } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Document doc = new Document(); doc.print(); doc.show(); } } Generic programming in Java Generics allow parameters for types, catching type errors at compile-time instead of runtime. // Generic Class class Box<T> { private T item; public void set(T t) { item = t; } public T get() { return item; } } // Generic Method public <E> void printArray(E[] array) { for(E element : array) { System.out.println(element); } } Advantages: Code can be reused for any object type while maintaining rigorous type safety without explicit casting. int total = list.size(); // Count System.out.println("Total: " + total + ", Has Banana: " + hasBanana); } } Packages: java.util is a built-in package. If we created package com.myutils; at the top, it would be user-defined.

Unit V: Collections Garbage Collection in Java Garbage Collection (GC) is the process by which Java programs perform automatic memory management, freeing up the heap by deleting objects that are no longer in use. An object becomes eligible for garbage collection when it is completely unreferenced (i.e., no live thread can access it). This happens if its reference is set to null , if it is created anonymously, or if references are reassigned. Garbage Collection and finalization in Java Garbage Collection automatically deallocates memory for objects that are no longer reachable. Eligibility: An object is eligible if its reference is set to null , reassigned, or created anonymously. finalize(): A method in the Object class historically called by the GC just before destroying the object to release non-Java resources. Deprecation: finalize() was deprecated in Java 9 because it is unpredictable, impacts performance, and can cause memory leaks if implemented poorly. Modern Alternatives: Use try-with-resources (implementing AutoCloseable ) for deterministic resource cleanup, or the java.lang.ref.Cleaner API.
